fine_trace.note: The attacker-controlled <xi:include href="t.txt" parse="text"/> element inside <a> is recognized as an XInclude node during phase 1 of xmlXIncludeProcessNode invoked from xmlTextReaderRead; its tree pointer is taken as the reference node.
The include element pointer cur is stored as ctxt->incTab[0]->ref, so the persistent reader XInclude context now aliases a document-tree node whose lifetime is controlled by the reader.

During phase 3 of the first processing the reader cleared XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE, so the include element is converted in place to XML_XINCLUDE_START and remains a child of <a>; incTab[0]->ref still points at it.

When the reader moves from <a> to the following sibling, tmp=<a> is not marked preserved, so the free decision is taken even though the XInclude context still references the XML_XINCLUDE_START node inside the subtree. The safety condition that should have held is that the node be preserved so this free is skipped.

xmlTextReaderFreeNode recursively frees the <a> subtree, releasing the XML_XINCLUDE_START node that ctxt->incTab[0]->ref still points to; the XInclude context is never informed, so incTab[0]->ref becomes a dangling pointer.

When the reader reaches the second <xi:include> element, xmlXIncludeProcessNode reuses the same context; phase 3 re-processes every ref from incBase=0, including ref 0 whose ref node was freed by the reader.
cur = ctxt->incTab[0]->ref is a dangling non-NULL pointer into freed memory; reading cur->type is a heap-use-after-free inside xmlXIncludeIncludeNode.
